findings.statement: CXCR2 transcripts in inflamed UC mucosa are almost entirely neutrophil (Gubatan 2026) [gene=CXCR2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.965]. In Smillie 2019, which has no neutrophils, the dominant lineage is T/NK (a background artefact) and it does not replicate across Garrido-Trigo 2023, Gubatan 2026 and GSE282122. After composition adjustment the change shrinks to [gene=CXCR2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.4409] (partly_composition). The top-ranked CXCR2 mostly marks neutrophil influx; any drug effect would act through neutrophil recruitment, not epithelial or stromal change.

CXCL8 is made by myeloid cells (replicated in Garrido-Trigo 2023, Gubatan 2026 and GSE282122) and by neutrophils in Gubatan 2026 [gene=CXCL8; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.873]. Its bulk increase loses significance after composition adjustment [gene=CXCL8; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_padj=0.0525] (verdict composition), so it is best read as a marker of myeloid and neutrophil influx. Adjustment may over-correct if resident cells are activated.

MMP1 is made by inflammatory fibroblasts (stromal lineage dominant in Smillie 2019 and replicated in all three other atlases), with little neutrophil contribution. The bulk change stays significant after adjustment [gene=MMP1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.2636] (partly_composition), so it is a tissue change. Visium deconvolution assigns most in-situ signal to inflammatory fibroblasts [gene=MMP1; type=spatial_visium_cell; source=DATASET:GSE189184; in_situ_contribution=0.568]. CosMx detection was at background.

DUOX2 is epithelial (enterocytes), with an epithelial share of [gene=DUOX2; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.947] in Smillie 2019, replicated in all three other atlases. It retains a strong change after composition adjustment [gene=DUOX2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3161] (partly_composition), so this is an intrinsic epithelial response, not influx. It has no drug yet.

CHI3L1 is stromal (inflammatory fibroblasts), with a stromal share of [gene=CHI3L1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; dominant_lineage_share=0.941] in Smillie 2019. The attribution replicates in Garrido-Trigo 2023 and GSE282122, but Gubatan 2026 calls it myeloid because neutrophils also contribute. The bulk change persists after adjustment [gene=CHI3L1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=1.3967].

AQP9 is myeloid in all four atlases, and neutrophils make most of its transcripts in Gubatan 2026 [gene=AQP9; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.92]. A smaller change remains after adjustment [gene=AQP9; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.8551] (partly_composition). It is mainly a marker of neutrophil influx.

TREM1 is myeloid in all four atlases, with neutrophils carrying most transcripts in Gubatan 2026 [gene=TREM1; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.894]. A change remains after adjustment [gene=TREM1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.6621] (partly_composition), so some of it is activation of myeloid cells and some is influx.

IDO1 is myeloid in Smillie 2019 (macrophages and DC1), replicated in Garrido-Trigo 2023 and GSE282122, while Gubatan 2026 assigns it to enterocytes, so the source is mixed myeloid and epithelial. Neutrophils contribute little. The change survives adjustment [gene=IDO1; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.8505] (partly_composition), which indicates a tissue-intrinsic induction.

CD274 (PD-L1) has a diffuse source (plasma cells, macrophages, epithelium; lineage share low) and neutrophils carry much of it in Gubatan 2026 [gene=CD274; type=sc_summary; source=DATASET:SCP259; neutrophil_share_inflamed=0.687]. The replication rule is met (myeloid in Garrido-Trigo 2023 and Gubatan 2026) but the attribution is weak. A change remains after adjustment [gene=CD274; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=0.4978].

HMGCS2 is down in UC and mostly not neutrophil-derived (an epithelial metabolic gene), and the loss persists after adjustment [gene=HMGCS2; type=composition_effect; source=ANALYSIS:composition; layer=rna; adjusted_log2fc=-0.8548] (partly_composition). It reflects a change inside the epithelium (loss of mature absorptive cells or butyrate metabolism), not influx.

caveats: Smillie 2019 captured no neutrophils, so lineage calls for neutrophil-derived genes (CXCR2, CXCR1) rely on Gubatan 2026; CXCR2 appears as T/NK in Smillie because of very sparse counts. CXCR1 shows the same neutrophil dominance (share 0.962, EV:sc_summary:450a602fd6f8) but was not analysed further.

Composition adjustment can over-correct: lineage scores also rise when resident cells are activated, so a lost signal (CXCL8) is not proof of pure influx, and retained signal is strong evidence of a tissue change.
Shares compare cell types, not tissue abundance; dissociation protocols enrich some fractions.
CosMx detection of MMP1 was at background and Visium spot co-variation is weaker evidence than single-cell data. Xenium did not cover MMP1.
Only a subset of the top 40 was analysed at cell level; the remaining chemokines, MMPs and S100 genes were checked only for neutrophil share (S100A8 high, MMP3 low).
